note.happening: Netflix closed at 58.1, up 2.41% on the day, but still in a downtrend below its 20-day (61.99), 50-day (66.96) and 200-day (79.82) averages, all falling. The only news was reported debate over the Netflix show 'The Altruists' and how it portrays FTX, which matters for buzz, not for the business. The next earnings report is due 2027-01-19.
note.business: The business is still strong. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) rose to 11.4B from 9.0B. Operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) rose to 31.3% from 29.14%. The share count fell 3.35% in a year. What is at risk is growth and how long the margin lasts. Quarterly sales growth slowed to 11.85% from 16.19% two quarters ago. The filings note that a 31% margin sits at the top of its 5-year range (17–31%), and peaks like that usually fade. Analysts cut this quarter's EPS (earnings per share) estimate to 0.68 from 0.73, a 7.3% cut in 30 days. Debt (12.7B) is higher than cash (8.2B), but cash flow covers it easily. The reported show debate changes sentiment only. It does not touch demand, margins, cash or competition.

worth.text: At 58.1 the stock trades at 16.5 times trailing earnings and 15.4 times next year's. Its price-to-sales ratio is 4.8, against a peer median of 6.5, and sits at the 18th percentile of its own 5-year range. A cash-flow model (DCF: today's value of future cash) gives 37.53 bear, 63.7 base and 76.06 bull. The own-history price-to-sales method gives 58.94 low to 122.15 high. Today's price assumes free cash flow starts growing at about 12.4% a year. At 10% starting growth the value is 52.77. At 20% it is 78.72. The gap between methods comes from the growth assumption: the bear case starts from analysts' 5% EPS growth, while the base and bull cases use the recent 15% sales growth. Margin matters too. If operating margin fell to 23%, the value would be 58.77, slightly above today's price. At 15% margin it would drop to 38.82.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow starts growing at 10% to 20% a year, close to the 12.4% the price implies, and operating margin does not fall much below 23%.
